title: spec-pack behaviors/progress.jsonl — implementation progress log (one entry per line)
description: Append-only coordination log for whoever implements the pack, including multi-agent implementers. This framework DEFINES THE SHAPE AND WRITES NOTHING. c9 seeds the file empty and excludes it from every regeneration and hash check — it is the one mutable file in the pack, owned entirely by the implementer. Current state is derived by replaying entries in order, not by mutating a record: concurrent writers appending is safe, whereas concurrent writers rewriting a mutable JSON file silently lose claims. Same discipline as nodes.jsonl/edges.jsonl. Deliberately absent: CI config, branching model, review gates, sprint structure, agent prompts — the substrate is specified, the process is not.

ts.description: ISO-8601, UTC. Ordering key when replaying. Ties broken by file line order.

part.description: Optional sub-unit within the behavior, if the implementer splits work further (e.g. 'api', 'ui', 'tests'). This framework deliberately does not define the split — the vocabulary is the implementer's, because how a behavior divides across a stack is a property of that stack, not of the legacy app.

event.description: claimed: this actor intends to work it (the mutual-exclusion primitive). released: claim given up without progress. started/done: work boundaries. blocked/unblocked: paused on an external dependency. abandoned: will not be done, needs a reason. note: free commentary, no state change.

actor.description: Who emitted this — an agent id, a username, a CI job. Required on every entry so a claim is always attributable.

lease_expires.description: For 'claimed': when the claim lapses if no further entry appears. Without this, a crashed agent's claim blocks a behavior forever. A replayer treats an expired claim as released. Choose a duration longer than a realistic unit of work.

reason.description: Required for 'blocked' and 'abandoned'. An abandoned behavior with no reason is indistinguishable from a dropped one, which is exactly the silent-loss failure this framework exists to prevent.

blocked_on.description: For 'blocked': BHV ids, or free-text external blockers.

ref.description: Optional pointer to where the work landed — a commit, PR, or branch. Not interpreted by anything here.
